clue.text: Farsi song or poem's kept back in expectation of complaint

indicators.note: kept back says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Persian poem is held back in anticipation of grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept back' turns SISONGORP, the run inside 'Farsi song or poem's', to read backwards; 'in' is only a link. 'Complaint' means an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's forecast of how an illness will run is the medical sense of this word.

clue.text: Poser sinks bottom right in the dessert!

indicators.note: sinks says one piece drops down into the middle of another

parts.note: pud is British slang for a pudding or dessert
on a map the bottom right corner is the south-east, SE

explanation.surface: Someone showing off plunges a spoon into the pudding at the lower corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom right' is the compass point SE (south-east), which sinks into PUD, British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretentious person putting on intellectual airs is a poser, in British slang.

clue.text: Steer dogs past wide swamp

indicators.note: to dog is to follow closely, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: over means past, finished
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide, a ball bowled out of reach
the helm is what steers a ship; to helm is to steer

explanation.surface: A musher guides the sled dogs beyond a broad marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' is a verb, to follow behind, not the animals pulling a sled; 'wide' is a cricket term.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp someone is to flood or overpower them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Healthy one performing great number

parts.note: healthy is read whimsically as not ill, non-ill
I is the Roman numeral one
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A fit person taking the stage gives a big number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Healthy' is split playfully into NON-ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A one followed by thirty zeros (or fifty-four in old British usage) is a huge quantity.

clue.text: One cracking gags —- or saying it's better not to?

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: gags as a verb means silences, stops from speaking
I is the Roman numeral one
or is the heraldic word for gold, giving golden

explanation.surface: A comedian telling jokes wonders whether keeping quiet would be wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gags' looks like jokes but is a verb, SILENCES; 'or' is heraldic gold, not the conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: This proverb holds that keeping quiet is wiser than speaking, so it says not talking is better.

clue.text: Boxers — one plucked hair, delivering unpleasant punishment

parts.note: boxers are boxer shorts
a harp is an instrument whose strings are plucked
a shock is a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: A boxer pulls out one of his rival's hairs, landing a nasty penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase was a 1980s British policy slogan for brief harsh detention of young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a brief, severe penalty meant to deter, especially for young offenders.

clue.text: Having nothing on end snake dance

indicators.note: on end says the change happens at the final letter of the snake

parts.note: a mamba is a venomous African snake
O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A snake with nothing on performs a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The final A of MAMBA is swapped for O; 'Having' is a link. The clue shares its words with 27 across, read differently.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban ballroom style is a lively Latin dance.

clue.text: Legal officer's bungle overlooking a fine, it arises

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to muff something is to bungle it
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: arises in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A lawyer's blunder in missing a penalty comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: One F (fine) is dropped from MUFF, then IT reads upwards as TI; the possessive 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam this is a scholar empowered to give rulings on religious law.

clue.text: Capital, singular, fur coats

indicators.note: coats means covers round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: mink is a prized fur
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: In the capital, a single fur coat stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' is a verb, MINK wrapping S.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Belarus.

clue.text: Sort of food almost everyone, surprisingly, eats these days

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so one piece swallows the other
surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected order
almost says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, these days

explanation.surface: Nowadays almost everyone eats some kind of processed food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E, 'surprisingly' scrambles what is left, and 'eats' swallows the era abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Food sold prepared so it needs only heating is described this way.

clue.text: Constant backing for different networks

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the joined pieces read backwards

parts.note: a LAN is a local area network; a rete is an anatomical network
rete is Latin for net, an anatomical network of vessels or nerves

explanation.surface: Support for varied broadcasters stays steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses LAN and RETE together; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Everlasting and unchanging is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Railing's causing injury

parts.note: the possessive 's is read as of
a railing is a fence

explanation.surface: A fence is causing someone harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railing's' is read as 'of fence'; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of this word is harm or wrong done to someone.

clue.text: Fastener to flourish when clipped

indicators.note: clipped means cut short at the end

parts.note: to do well is to flourish

explanation.surface: A clip to fasten things grows when cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: DO WELL loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden peg used to join pieces of furniture holds parts together.

clue.text: Particular person, on reflection briefly, short and plump for a queen

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, read backwards
briefly says the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: tiny means very short
to plump for is to choose, pick
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: A fussy person, thinking quickly, picks a queen who is small and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts TINY to TIN and 'on reflection' turns it to NIT. 'Particular' means fussy, not specific; 'plump' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fussy, pedantic fault-finder is someone very particular about small details.

clue.text: He died some distance from China, pierced by English daggers

indicators.note: pierced by says a piece is stuck into the middle

parts.note: ob., obiit, is Latin for he died, seen on gravestones
a li is a Chinese unit of distance

explanation.surface: A man died far from China, stabbed by English daggers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daggers' are printers' marks, not knives; ob. appears on old gravestones.
explanation.definitionFit: These printed dagger marks, used for footnotes or doubtful passages, are typographers' daggers.

clue.text: Ranks novel about a poorly revolutionary, describing it?

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the piece reads backwards
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: novel means new
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: Lines of people circle a sick revolutionary in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and the illness inside the novel piece (N-AILL-EW) and 'revolutionary' turns that round to WELLIAN. 'it' is the revolution gone sour in the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the totalitarian world of Animal Farm and 1984, novels of revolution gone wrong.

clue.text: Nil-all and one-each replays: senseless repetition

indicators.note: replays suggests the pieces are played again in a different order

parts.note: O is zero, nil
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Football results of 0-0 and 1-1 lead to replays and dull repetition.
explanation.walkthrough: Draws in British cup football go to a replay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the clinical term for automatically repeating words just heard, without meaning.

clue.text: Muck in conclusion I'm surprised to find in ground

indicators.note: in places the joined pieces inside the other piece

parts.note: land is ground
the end is the conclusion
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Surprised to find dirt in the ground at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muck in' is British for joining in with work.
explanation.definitionFit: To muck in, a British idiom, is to pitch in and help with a shared task.

clue.text: Movement at grass-roots level a great electoral success

definitions.meaning: a slip of earth, read playfully as a movement of the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'grass-roots' suggests local politics; here it is literal earth sliding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a collapse of a hillside and a crushing election win.

clue.text: Turning back on immorality, a flash western Lothario

indicators.note: turning back says the whole string of pieces reads backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning
sin is immorality
a mo, a moment, is a flash

explanation.surface: Turning his back on vice, a showy cowboy plays the seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning back' reverses RE, SIN, A, MO and W together. 'flash' is a noun, a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a seducer in an old play, is the byword for a habitual seducer of women.

clue.text: Spoon-feed butter

definitions.meaning: one that butts, as a female goat does

explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is read as one who butts, a she-goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to over-protect and a female goat, which butts.

clue.text: Bringing comfort with pound, as loan shark's cross for a second

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: usurious describes a loan shark's excessive interest
S is the abbreviation for second
X is a cross

explanation.surface: Pounds paid with crosses for a loan shark make life comfy.
explanation.walkthrough: X takes the place of the first S in USURIOUS; 'with' and 'as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sumptuous and opulent gives great comfort and ease.

clue.text: Noble element love turning up to vote

indicators.note: to says this piece is attached to the end of the other

parts.note: X is the mark put on a ballot to vote

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: love in scoring means none, nothing

explanation.surface: Lovers are turning out to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: NONE reads upwards as ENON, added to X.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the noble gases, the unreactive elements.

clue.text: Rep leaves complaint, making member of family carp

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so these letters go

parts.note: a reproach is a complaint or rebuke

explanation.surface: A salesman drops a grievance, making a family member grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like a verb, to complain; it is the fish family.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater fish belongs to the cyprinid, or carp, family.

clue.text: Oral promise: that would-be bride hopes to make it up!

definitions.text: that would-be bride hopes to make it up!

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: I'll is a promise, a vow to do something

explanation.surface: A vow made out loud: the hope of a bride-to-be.
explanation.walkthrough: A bride hopes to walk up it in church; I'll and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The church passage a bride walks up to be married is what she hopes to go up.

clue.text: Likelihood team's opening pair have got out?

indicators.note: the first two letters are dismissed, like openers out in cricket

parts.note: an eleven is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: What are the odds that the team's two openers are out?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a team is an eleven; its opening pair of letters goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Even odds, where an outcome is as likely as not, describes a fifty-fifty chance.

clue.text: Abbreviated description of, say, Broadway's old tavern court

parts.note: Broadway is in New York, abbreviated as in NY
Broadway is a road, abbreviated as a Rd

explanation.surface: A short account of Broadway's historic pub courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadway is described as 'in NY, a Rd'.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtyard of an old coaching inn, where coaches drew up, was its yard.

clue.text: Glass, china blocks joined between the edges

indicators.note: blocks means sits in the way of, inside the other piece
between the edges takes the letters inside the first and last

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: Glass and china blocks are stuck together between the borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between the edges' strips the ends of 'joined'. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an opalescent, milky semi-translucent glass.

clue.text: Last of course to go out for the interval

definitions.text: Last of course to go out
definitions.meaning: on a golf course the outward half is the first nine holes, ending at this one
a musical interval spanning an octave plus a second

explanation.walkthrough: In golf, the front nine holes are 'going out'; the final one of those is this hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a golf hole closing the front nine and a musical interval.

clue.text: Having nothing on ends snake dance

indicators.note: dance suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A snake dances with nothing on its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Same words as 6 across with 'ends' for 'end'; here 'dance' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed is the state of having no clothes on.
